'''''Allium sphaerocephalon''''' is a plant species in the [[Amaryllidaceae|Amaryllis family]] known as '''round-headed leek''', '''round-headed garlic''', '''ball-head onion''', and other variations on these names. '''Drumstick allium''' is another common name applied to this species. Some publications use the alternate spelling ''Allium sphaerocephalum''.<ref>E.g. {{Citation |last=Mathew |first=Brian |year=1978 |title=The Larger Bulbs |publication-place=London |publisher=B.T. Batsford (in association with the Royal Horticultural Society) |isbn=978-0-7134-1246-8 }}</ref> It is a [[bulb]]ous [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]].

''Allium sphaerocephalon'' is found in the wild across all parts of Europe except in the northern and western countries ([[Scotland]], [[Ireland]], [[Netherlands]], [[Scandinavia]], and the [[Baltic States]]).<ref name="Davies1992"/><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=allium+sphaerocephalon Altervista Flora Italiana, Schede di botanica, ''Allium sphaerocephalon'']</ref> Its native range extends to northern Africa and to western Asia as far east as [[Iran]].<ref name="ravenisgod">[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=e132 Missouri Botanical Garden, Gardening Help, ''Allium sphaerocephalon'']</ref> It is also reportedly naturalised in [[New York State]] in the United States.<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Allium%20sphaerocephalon.png Biota of North America Program, ''Allium sphaerocephalon'']</ref> In [[England]] it grows wild only in the [[Avon Gorge]] so is known locally as the '''Bristol onion'''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/centenary/look/cabinet/bristol-onion.html |title=Bristol Onion |publisher=Bristol University |access-date=2014-10-08}}</ref>

The species is prized by gardeners because of its striking floral display. The spherical "[[Head (botany)|head]]" (technically an [[umbel]]) is borne on a long [[Scape (botany)|scape]], up to 50 cm in height, usually in July. It can contain hundreds of deep reddish purple flowers.<ref name="ravenisgod"/>

The [[specific epithet]] ''sphaerocephalon'' derives from ancient Greek, meaning "spherical head".

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/870/i-Allium-sphaerocephalon-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Allium sphaerocephalon''
| publisher=Royal Horticultural Society | date=2016 | access-date=5 January 2018}}</ref>

==Description==
''Allium sphaerocephalon'' produces egg-shaped bulbs. Small [[bulblet]]s are present under the outer layer of the stem (making the plant potentially [[Invasive species|invasive]] when grown in gardens). Flowers are borne on a [[Scape (botany)|scape]] up to 50 cm in height, in a spherical to egg-shaped [[umbels|umbel]], 1–6 cm in diameter, tightly packed with many flowers crowded together. The relatively small size of the umbel relative to the height of the stem makes this one of those described as "drumstick alliums". Individual flowers are reddish-purple and are occasionally replaced by bulbils (again making this a potentially invasive species).<ref name="Davies1992">{{Citation |last=Davies |first=Dilys |year=1992 |title=Alliums : the ornamental onions |publication-place=London |publisher=B.T. Batsford (in association with the Hardy Plant Society) |isbn=978-0-7134-7030-7 }}, p. 135</ref>
